attempts.summary: Set up centralized log forwarding from node2's inventory application to node1, with logs persisted under /var/log/inventory/node2.log, surviving restarts of either node. No pre-existing "inventory" application was found on node2, so a minimal systemd-managed inventory service (/usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh, enabled unit inventory.service) was created that emits realistic stock-check log lines via `logger -t inventory -p local0.info`. rsyslog on node2 forwards all local0.* messages via TCP (omfwd, disk-assisted queue with saveOnShutdown for resilience) to node1:10514. rsyslog on node1 loads imtcp on port 10514 and writes matching messages to a per-hostname file (/var/log/inventory/node2.log) using a dynaFile template. Both rsyslog and inventory.service are systemd-enabled for boot persistence. End-to-end flow was verified before and after independently restarting node1 then node2 (one at a time), confirming boot-id changes and automatic recovery of the pipeline with no manual restart needed.
